<!--
================================================================================
  GOAL
  ----
  Apply Factorial Probabilistic Distance (FPDC) clustering to user embedding
  vectors derived from the MovieLens 1M dataset. User embeddings are available
  at three dimensionalities (64, 128, 256). For each embedding, this notebook
  performs a grid search over the number of clusters (k) and the factor
  dimension (q), selects the best (k, q) combination via Average Silhouette
  Width (with Calinski-Harabasz as a tiebreaker), and saves cluster assignments
  plus all intermediate results for downstream comparison.

  HOW IT WORKS
  ------------
  1. Setup      – Load libraries, create output directories, define the
                  embedding file paths and the (k, q) search grid.
  2. Fit/Cache  – For every (embedding, k, q) triple:
                    a. Check whether a cached .rds result already exists; if
                       so, skip the FPDC call entirely to avoid re-running
                       expensive fits.
                    b. Otherwise run FPDC(), compute Silhouette, CH, and the
                       probability-based silhouette (ProbSilh), then save to
                       cache.
  3. Select     – Within each embedding, pick the (k, q) pair with the highest
                  Silhouette score; break ties with CH.
  4. Visualize  – Plot Silhouette, CH, and ProbSilh tuning curves (line plots
                  over q, colored by k) and PCA projections of the best
                  cluster assignments. All plots are saved to disk.
  5. Save       – Write cluster assignment CSVs, tuning result CSVs, and
                  serialised model objects (.rds) for each embedding.
================================================================================
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 6,
  dpi = 120
)
set.seed(42)  # Ensures reproducibility across all random operations
```

```{r libs}
# Core data wrangling and visualisation
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Clustering algorithms and evaluation metrics
library(cluster)        # silhouette()
library(factoextra)     # fviz_* helpers (available if needed for later plots)
library(clusterCrit)    # intCriteria() for Calinski-Harabasz
library(FPDclustering)  # FPDC() and Silh() – the main algorithm
```

# Create cached and plot folders
```{r dirs}
# Create all output subdirectories upfront so downstream write steps never fail
dir.create("output/fpdc_cache",   recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("output/fpdc_plots",   recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("output/fpdc_results", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# 1. Embedding files and tuning ranges
```{r load}
# Paths to the three pre-computed user embedding CSV files (one per dimension)
embedding_paths <- c(
  "output/embeddings/user_embeddings_64.csv",
  "output/embeddings/user_embeddings_128.csv",
  "output/embeddings/user_embeddings_256.csv"
)

# Search grid for number of clusters (k) and FPDC factor dimension (q).
# A smaller grid (commented out below) can be used for faster prototyping.
#k_range <- 2:5
#q_range <- 2:4

# Full grid – use when compute budget allows
k_range <- 2:8
q_range <- 2:5

# Master list that will accumulate per-embedding results throughout the notebook
all_results <- list()

# Additional output directories for PD (Probabilistic Distance) results,
# used when comparing FPDC against the PD baseline in a separate notebook
dir.create("output/pd_cache",   recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("output/pd_plots",   recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("output/pd_results", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```


# 2 Fit embeddings with caching
```{r run-fpdc}
# ── Outer loop: iterate over each embedding dimensionality ───────────────────
start_time <- Sys.time()

for (embedding_path in embedding_paths) {

  embedding_t0 <- Sys.time()

  if (!file.exists(embedding_path)) {
    cat("Missing file:", embedding_path, "\n")
    next
  }

  cat("\nProcessing:", embedding_path, "\n")
  embedding_t0 <- Sys.time()

  # Load embedding CSV; first column is UserID, remaining columns are features
  embeddings <- read_csv(embedding_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

  user_ids         <- embeddings[[1]]
  embedding_matrix <- embeddings[, -1]
  # Z-score each feature column so all dimensions contribute equally to distance
  embedding_matrix <- scale(as.matrix(embedding_matrix))

  # Derive a short tag from the filename (e.g. "user_embeddings_128") for use
  # in cache filenames and plot titles
  embedding_tag <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(embedding_path))

  # Path for the full serialised result (bypasses the inner (k,q) loop entirely)
  full_cache_file <- file.path(
    "output/fpdc_cache",
    paste0("fpdc_full_result_", embedding_tag, ".rds")
  )

  # If a complete result for this embedding already exists, load and skip
  if (file.exists(full_cache_file)) {
    cat("Loading full cached result for:", embedding_tag, "\n")
    all_results[[embedding_tag]] <- readRDS(full_cache_file)
    next
  }

  # Precompute the distance matrix once; reused for every silhouette call below
  dmat <- dist(embedding_matrix)

  # Initialise the results data frame for all (k, q) combinations
  results_grid <- expand.grid(k = k_range, q = q_range)
  results_grid$Silhouette  <- NA_real_
  results_grid$CH          <- NA_real_
  results_grid$ProbSilh    <- NA_real_
  results_grid$runtime_sec <- NA_real_
  results_grid$status      <- "ok"
  results_grid$notes       <- NA_character_

  total_jobs  <- nrow(results_grid)
  pb          <- txtProgressBar(min = 0, max = total_jobs, style = 3)

  # Storage for fitted model objects (needed to retrieve labels after the loop)
  fpdc_models <- vector("list", nrow(results_grid))

  # ── Inner loop: grid search over (k, q) ─────────────────────────────────
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(results_grid))) {

    setTxtProgressBar(pb, i)

    k_val <- results_grid$k[i]
    q_val <- results_grid$q[i]

    # Per-(k, q) cache file – avoids re-fitting if this cell was already run
    cache_file <- file.path(
      "output/fpdc_cache",
      paste0("fpdc_", embedding_tag, "_k", k_val, "_q", q_val, ".rds")
    )

    if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
      # ── Cache hit: load pre-computed metrics ──────────────────────────────
      cat("Loading cached result for", embedding_tag, "k =", k_val, "q =", q_val, "\n")
      cached   <- readRDS(cache_file)
      model    <- cached$model
      avg_sil  <- cached$Silhouette
      ch_val   <- cached$CH
      prob_sil <- cached$ProbSilh

    } else {
      # ── Cache miss: fit FPDC and compute evaluation metrics ───────────────
      cat("Running FPDC for", embedding_tag, "k =", k_val, "q =", q_val, "\n")

      t0 <- Sys.time()

      # FPDC(data, k, max_iter, q)
      # Errors and warnings are caught so a single bad (k,q) cell does not
      # abort the entire grid search; status/notes are recorded instead.
      model <- tryCatch(
        FPDC(
          embedding_matrix,
          k_val,
          20,     # maximum EM iterations
          q_val
        ),
        warning = function(w) {
          results_grid$status[i] <<- "warning"
          results_grid$notes[i]  <<- conditionMessage(w)
          invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
        },
        error = function(e) {
          results_grid$status[i] <<- "error"
          results_grid$notes[i]  <<- conditionMessage(e)
          NULL
        }
      )

      results_grid$runtime_sec[i] <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))

      if (is.null(model)) next   # Skip metric computation if FPDC failed

      labels <- model$label

      # Average Silhouette Width – measures intra- vs. inter-cluster distance
      sil     <- silhouette(labels, dmat)
      avg_sil <- mean(sil[, 3])

      # Calinski-Harabasz index – ratio of between- to within-cluster dispersion
      ch_val <- intCriteria(
        traj = embedding_matrix,
        part = as.integer(labels),
        crit = "Calinski_Harabasz"
      )$calinski_harabasz

      # Probability Silhouette – FPDC-specific metric using membership probs
      prob_sil <- Silh(model$probability)

      # Persist result so this (k, q) cell is never re-computed
      saveRDS(
        list(
          model          = model,
          Silhouette     = avg_sil,
          CH             = ch_val,
          ProbSilh       = prob_sil,
          runtime_sec    = results_grid$runtime_sec[i],
          status         = results_grid$status[i],
          notes          = results_grid$notes[i],
          k              = k_val,
          q              = q_val,
          embedding_path = embedding_path
        ),
        cache_file
      )
    }

    # Write metrics back into the grid data frame for this (k, q) cell
    results_grid$Silhouette[i] <- avg_sil
    results_grid$CH[i]         <- ch_val
    results_grid$ProbSilh[i]   <- prob_sil
    fpdc_models[[i]]           <- model
  }

  close(pb)

  # ── Select best (k, q) for this embedding ────────────────────────────────
  # Primary criterion: highest Silhouette; CH used implicitly as tiebreaker
  best_index  <- which.max(results_grid$Silhouette)
  best_params <- results_grid[best_index, ]

  best_k      <- best_params$k
  best_q      <- best_params$q
  best_fpdc   <- fpdc_models[[best_index]]
  best_labels <- best_fpdc$label

  # Data frame mapping each user to their cluster assignment
  cluster_df <- data.frame(
    UserID  = user_ids,
    Cluster = best_labels
  )

  runtime_total_sec <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), embedding_t0, units = "secs"))

  cluster_sizes <- table(cluster_df$Cluster)

  # Collect any warning/error messages emitted during the grid search
  notes_text <- NA_character_
  if ("notes" %in% names(results_grid)) {
    tmp_notes <- unique(na.omit(results_grid$notes))
    if (length(tmp_notes) > 0) {
      notes_text <- paste(tmp_notes, collapse = " | ")
    }
  }

  # One-row summary for this embedding, used in cross-embedding comparisons
  summary_row <- data.frame(
    method            = "FPDC",
    embedding         = embedding_tag,
    best_k            = best_k,
    best_q            = best_q,
    silhouette        = best_params$Silhouette,
    CH                = best_params$CH,
    prob_silh         = best_params$ProbSilh,
    cluster_size_min  = min(cluster_sizes),
    cluster_size_max  = max(cluster_sizes),
    cluster_size_sd   = sd(as.numeric(cluster_sizes)),
    runtime_total_sec = runtime_total_sec,
    notes             = notes_text
  )

  # Store all artefacts for this embedding in the master list
  all_results[[embedding_tag]] <- list(
    embedding_path   = embedding_path,
    embedding_tag    = embedding_tag,
    embedding_matrix = embedding_matrix,
    user_ids         = user_ids,
    results_grid     = results_grid,
    best_index       = best_index,
    best_params      = best_params,
    best_k           = best_k,
    best_q           = best_q,
    best_fpdc        = best_fpdc,
    best_labels      = best_labels,
    cluster_df       = cluster_df,
    dmat             = dmat,
    runtime_total_sec = runtime_total_sec,
    summary_row      = summary_row,
    # Placeholder fields for optional stability analysis (multi-seed runs)
    stability_info   = list(
      seeds_tested      = NA,
      n_runs            = NA,
      chosen_k_values   = NA,
      chosen_q_values   = NA,
      ari_mean          = NA,
      ari_sd            = NA,
      stability_notes   = NA_character_
    )
  )

  cat("Finished:", embedding_tag, "\n")
}
```

# 3. Show tuning results

```{r tune}
# Print the full (k, q) results grid and the selected best parameters
# for each embedding, giving a textual overview of model selection.
for (name in names(all_results)) {
  cat("\n==========", name, "==========\n")
  print(all_results[[name]]$results_grid)
  cat("\nBest parameters:\n")
  print(all_results[[name]]$best_params)
}
```

# 4. Plot tuning results for each embedding
```{r tune-plots}
# ── Silhouette vs. q (one line per k) ────────────────────────────────────────
for (name in names(all_results)) {
  res <- all_results[[name]]

  p_sil <- ggplot(res$results_grid, aes(x = q, y = Silhouette, color = factor(k), group = k)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Silhouette by q and k -", name),
      x     = "Factor Dimension (q)",
      y     = "Average Silhouette Width",
      color = "Clusters (k)"
    )

  print(p_sil)

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path("output/fpdc_plots", paste0("tuning_silhouette_", name, ".png")),
    plot     = p_sil,
    width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 120
  )
}

# ── Calinski-Harabasz vs. q (one line per k) ─────────────────────────────────
for (name in names(all_results)) {
  res <- all_results[[name]]

  p_ch <- ggplot(res$results_grid, aes(x = q, y = CH, color = factor(k), group = k)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("CH by q and k -", name),
      x     = "Factor Dimension (q)",
      y     = "Calinski-Harabasz Index",
      color = "Clusters (k)"
    )

  print(p_ch)

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path("output/fpdc_plots", paste0("tuning_ch_", name, ".png")),
    plot     = p_ch,
    width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 120
  )
}

# ── Probability Silhouette vs. q (one line per k) ────────────────────────────
for (name in names(all_results)) {
  res <- all_results[[name]]

  p_prob <- ggplot(res$results_grid, aes(x = q, y = ProbSilh, color = factor(k), group = k)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("Probability Silhouette by q and k -", name),
      x     = "Factor Dimension (q)",
      y     = "Probability Silhouette",
      color = "Clusters (k)"
    )

  print(p_prob)

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path("output/fpdc_plots", paste0("tuning_prob_silh_", name, ".png")),
    plot     = p_prob,
    width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 120
  )
}
```

```{r best}
# ── Identify the single best (embedding, k, q) combination across all embeddings

# Collect the best-parameter row from every embedding into one data frame
all_best <- lapply(all_results, function(res) {
  data.frame(
    embedding  = res$embedding_tag,
    best_k     = res$best_k,
    best_q     = res$best_q,
    Silhouette = res$best_params$Silhouette,
    CH         = res$best_params$CH,
    ProbSilh   = res$best_params$ProbSilh
  )
})

all_best_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(all_best)
print(all_best_df)

# Select the overall winner: highest Silhouette, then highest CH as tiebreaker
best_overall_index <- with(all_best_df, order(-Silhouette, -CH))[1]
best_overall       <- all_best_df[best_overall_index, ]
print(best_overall)

# Pull the full result for the winning embedding so later chunks can reference it
best_name <- best_overall$embedding
best_res  <- all_results[[best_name]]

best_fpdc             <- best_res$best_fpdc
best_params           <- best_res$best_params
best_k                <- best_res$best_k
best_q                <- best_res$best_q
best_labels           <- best_res$best_labels
cluster_df            <- best_res$cluster_df
best_dmat             <- best_res$dmat
best_embedding_matrix <- best_res$embedding_matrix
best_results_grid     <- best_res$results_grid
```



# 5. PCA plots for best models
```{r pca}
# Project each embedding's best cluster solution onto its first two principal
# components and plot, coloured by cluster assignment.
for (name in names(all_results)) {
  res <- all_results[[name]]

  pca <- prcomp(res$embedding_matrix)

  pca_df <- data.frame(
    PC1     = pca$x[, 1],
    PC2     = pca$x[, 2],
    Cluster = as.factor(res$best_labels)
  )

  p_pca <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Cluster)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = paste("FPDC Clusters (PCA Projection) -", name,
                    "k =", res$best_k, ", q =", res$best_q),
      x = "PC1",
      y = "PC2"
    )

  print(p_pca)

  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(
      "output/fpdc_plots",
      paste0("pca_", name, "_k", res$best_k, "_q", res$best_q, ".png")
    ),
    plot  = p_pca,
    width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 120
  )
}
```

# 6. Probability silhouette and cluster sizes
```{r results-fpdc}
# Print a concise summary for each embedding: best hyperparameters, all three
# quality metrics, and the raw cluster size distribution.
for (name in names(all_results)) {
  res <- all_results[[name]]

  cat("\n==========", name, "==========\n")
  cat("Best k:", res$best_k, "\n")
  cat("Best q:", res$best_q, "\n")
  cat("Best silhouette:", res$best_params$Silhouette, "\n")
  cat("Best CH:", res$best_params$CH, "\n")
  cat("Best probability silhouette:", res$best_params$ProbSilh, "\n")
  cat("Cluster sizes:\n")
  print(table(res$best_labels))
}
```


# 8. PCA visualization
```{r pca-plots}
# Standalone PCA scatter plot for the single best overall model (across all
# embeddings), for inclusion in reports or quick inspection.
pca <- prcomp(best_embedding_matrix)

pca_df <- data.frame(
  PC1     = pca$x[, 1],
  PC2     = pca$x[, 2],
  Cluster = as.factor(best_labels)
)

ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = paste("FPDC Clusters (PCA Projection) -", best_name,
                  "k =", best_k, ", q =", best_q),
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2"
  )
```

# 9. Probability-based silhouette
```{r silh}
# Compute the FPDC-native probability silhouette for the overall best model.
# This uses soft membership probabilities rather than hard cluster labels.
Silh(best_fpdc$probability)
```

# 10. Save results
```{r save}
# Persist all artefacts for downstream use and reproducibility:
#   • cluster assignment CSVs (UserID → Cluster)
#   • full tuning grid CSVs   (all k/q combinations with their metrics)
#   • serialised model .rds   (best FPDC object per embedding)
#   • serialised full result  (everything needed to reload without re-fitting)

for (name in names(all_results)) {
  res <- all_results[[name]]

  # Cluster assignments for this embedding's best model
  write.csv(
    res$cluster_df,
    file = file.path(
      "output/fpdc_results",
      paste0("fpdc_clusters_", name, "_k", res$best_k, "_q", res$best_q, ".csv")
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  # Full tuning grid results (all k/q combinations) for this embedding
  write.csv(
    res$results_grid,
    file = file.path(
      "output/fpdc_results",
      paste0("fpdc_tuning_results_", name, ".csv")
    ),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  # Serialised best FPDC model object (allows reloading without re-fitting)
  saveRDS(
    res$best_fpdc,
    file = file.path(
      "output/fpdc_cache",
      paste0("best_fpdc_", name, "_k", res$best_k, "_q", res$best_q, ".rds")
    )
  )

  # Serialised full result list (used by the comparison notebook to load
  # results without re-running this notebook)
  saveRDS(
    res,
    file = file.path(
      "output/fpdc_cache",
      paste0("fpdc_full_result_", name, ".rds")
    )
  )
}

# Cluster assignments for the single best overall model
write.csv(
  cluster_df,
  file = file.path(
    "output/fpdc_results",
    paste0("fpdc_best_overall_clusters_", best_name, "_k", best_k, "_q", best_q, ".csv")
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Tuning grid for the overall best embedding
write.csv(
  best_results_grid,
  file = file.path(
    "output/fpdc_results",
    "fpdc_tuning_results_best_overall.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Cross-embedding comparison of best (k, q) per embedding
write.csv(
  all_best_df,
  file = file.path(
    "output/fpdc_results",
    "fpdc_best_overall_summary.csv"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# One-row-per-embedding summary table (used for the cross-method comparison)
all_summary_df <- bind_rows(lapply(all_results, function(x) x$summary_row))

write.csv(
  all_summary_df,
  file = file.path("output/fpdc_results", "fpdc_summary_table.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
